answers.q1: Cargo (Rust's built-in package manager and build tool; the workspace requires Rust 1.96 or newer, and no rust-toolchain file pins one). Install dependencies from the repo root with: cargo fetch (building with cargo build --workspace also downloads them).
answers.q2: cargo test --workspace (this is what CI runs; the README's cargo test --all is an older form of the same thing). CI also runs cargo test --workspace --features unstable-index and cargo test --workspace --features pcre2 as separate passes.
answers.q3: cargo test --test integration regression:: (tests/regression.rs is not its own Cargo target: autotests = false, and it is compiled as the regression module of the single 'integration' target from tests/tests.rs, so the test name filter is needed).
answers.q4: cargo fmt --all --check (the rustfmt CI job) and RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace (the docs CI job). CI does not run clippy.
answers.q5: None are vendored: there is no vendor/ directory and every crate under crates/ is first-party workspace code. Cargo.lock is tool-generated and should be changed only through cargo commands, not by hand. The gitignored /deployment directory and build outputs under target/ are generated and should not be edited.

q1.reason: Cargo with `cargo fetch` (and mentions cargo build also downloads), matching the accept criteria.

q2.reason: Gives `cargo test --workspace`, which matches CI, and the extra feature passes are harmless.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test integration regression::` exactly matches an accepted command and the explanation is correct.

q4.reason: Gives `cargo fmt --all --check` plus the cargo doc command, and correctly says CI doesn't run clippy.

q5.reason: Correctly says nothing is vendored and names Cargo.lock and target/, but also claims a gitignored /deployment directory is generated, which is not in the ground truth.
